title: C Y P two C nineteen, clopidogrel, and proton pump inhibitors

segs.text: Section twelve. C Y P two C nineteen, the star seventeen gain of function, clopidogrel, and proton pump inhibitors. This enzyme drives two opposite clinical stories. The point is to reason from variant, to enzyme function, to drug handling, to patient outcome. Its substrates are slightly acidic drugs, such as proton pump inhibitors, fluoxetine, sertraline, and diazepam. There are over thirty alleles, but four drive most phenotypes, which run from poor and intermediate to extensive and ultrarapid.

Star two and star three carry a premature stop codon, so no active enzyme is made. Star seventeen is the first gain of function variant in this lecture. She said, The reason for that is this snip is located in the upstream region of the gene where the machinery for expressing the gene sits down on the gene and starts its work. So more C Y P two C nineteen is made and total activity rises. Star seventeen does not change the enzyme's shape, and it is not extra gene copies.

Clopidogrel is a prodrug that C Y P two C nineteen helps activate, so both directions are dangerous. A star two or star three carrier makes too little active drug and keeps sticky platelets, which is therapeutic failure. A star seventeen carrier makes too much and is over anticoagulated. That is why she said, clopidogrel is a drug for which we should be genotyping people for their two C nineteen status.

With proton pump inhibitors, being a poor metabolizer is good. Low activity keeps drug levels higher, which raises gastric p H more and improves cure rates. This is safe because the therapeutic index of these drugs is very wide. She said, When you had the low activity version of the enzyme increasing drug blood concentrations, you had better cure rates. In the figure from Furuta and colleagues, two thousand four, which used lansoprazole, poor metabolizers had the highest area under the curve and the highest gastric p H, not the extensive metabolizers. The assigned reading, Furuta and colleagues in nineteen ninety eight, treated sixty two Japanese patients with omeprazole plus amoxicillin, and its authors state that plasma omeprazole levels were not measured.

The same high levels are a problem with the other substrates. A poor metabolizer on a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor or on diazepam has more adverse drug responses, and more sedation with diazepam. So the poor metabolizer benefits only where the therapeutic index is wide, as with proton pump inhibitors.
